title: Target anatomy
view: Transverse section of the right buttock at the level of the ischial tuberosity and greater trochanter, prone, under a transverse probe, as on ultrasound: medial (ischial tuberosity) on the image left, lateral (greater trochanter) on the right. Composition after NYSORA's gluteal plate (concept only).
teachingPoint: The sciatic nerve is a flat oval midway between the ischial tuberosity and the greater trochanter, under gluteus maximus; the needle comes from lateral to its lateral edge and the spread surrounds it in the plane.
claims: Ischial tuberosity medial, greater trochanter lateral, nerve midway between them deep to gluteus maximus (record).
Nerve lies on quadratus femoris in the plane under gluteus maximus, in its own fascial sheath (standard anatomy; house style for the sheath).
Needle in-plane from lateral to the lateral edge of the nerve (record: in-plane; NYSORA: lateral to medial).
Teal: spread around the nerve in the plane (record: inject around it).
Typical adult depths: nerve about 5 cm deep (schematic).
Labels: Gluteus maximus, Sciatic nerve, Ischial tuberosity, Greater trochanter, Quadratus femoris.

geometry.why: needle in-plane from the lateral end
tip at the lateral edge, not into the nerve
